newsitem.title: UK: UK brewing stocks climb on accounting proposals.
newsitem.headline: UK brewing stocks climb on accounting proposals.

text.p: UK brewing stocks climbed on Thursday following the release of a discussion paper from the Accounting Standards Board (ASB) on the treatment of fixed assets which is likely to impact earnings among brewing companies less than many had feared, traders said.
In the light of the rule changes, UBS had upgraded its stance on the sector to "buy" from "sell", said market sources, with other houses also said to have made positive comments.
Whitbread was trading 17-1/2p higher at 715-1/2p by mid-afternoon with Bass up 15-1/2p at 794p and Scottish & Newcastle up 8-1/2p at 649-1/2p.

The discussion paper, which sets out proposals on the valuation and depreciation of tangible fixed assets, is the first stage toward the development of a new accounting standard on the subject. "Its not as bad as the market feared," said Mark Puleikis, an analyst at Merrill Lynch. "The worst case scenario would have been writing fixed assets down to zero. Instead what this could mean is writing down to a residual value, which still needs to be clarified."
But the implication is that the effect on earnings is theoretically half what it could have been," said Puleikis.
"A number of companies would simply put in their accounts that they did not need to depreciate because their capital spend was high enough," said Alan Cook, technical director at the ASB.

"There are some industries like hotels or brewers who argue because they are continually refurbishing they don't need to think about depreciating. In fact there are only a very small number of assets that are so unique that you can't replace them," said Cook.
"If you depreciate down to residual value, that price ought to be in the same terms as the price you originally paid for it."
Comments from the industry on the ASB discussion paper are due by January 17.
